name: Zaporozhian Cossacks
alt: Free Lands of the Lower Zaporozhian Host

successors.name: Russian Empire
successors.text: the Zaporozhian lands, annexed to the Novorossiya Governorate by the manifesto of 3 August 1775

successors.name: Danubian Sich
successors.text: the Danube Delta, where the fleeing Cossacks 'formed the new Danubian Sich' (to 1828)

capitals.name: Chortomlyk Sich (mouth of the Chortomlyk River)
Kamianka Sich (mouth of the Kamianka River)

ledger.x: 1552: the Zaporozhian Sich arises on the lower Dnieper beyond the rapids.

c. 1564: the Host's seat moves to the Tomakivka Sich, an island in the Dnieper near Marhanets (table: c. 1564-1593), after Khortytsia was destroyed in 1558; the page dates no Sich for the years between.
1593: 'The Tatars razed the Tomakivka Sich'; the Bazavluk Sich (1593-1638) becomes the seat.
1639: the Mykytyn Sich (1639-1652) replaces the Bazavluk Sich, 'destroyed by a Polish expeditionary force' in 1638.
1652: 'The Chortomlyk Sich was built at the mouth of the Chortomlyk River' (table: 1652-1709); Khmelnytsky had captured the Mykytyn Sich in 1648.
1709: the Chortomlyk Sich is destroyed and the Kamianka Sich is founded at the mouth of the Kamianka River (table: 1709-1711).
1711: the Kamianka Sich is destroyed 'by the Russian government'; the Cossacks flee to the Crimean Khanate and found the Oleshky Sich (1711-1728), under Crimean-Ottoman protection.
c. 1728: a Kamianka Sich is again the seat (table: c. 1728-1734; the table also lists a Chortomlyk Sich for 1728-1730), leaving Oleshky.

1734: 'In 1734, they were allowed to return to the Russian Empire' and built the Nova Sich near the former Chortomlyk Sich (1734-1775); the Cossacks page adds that they 'regained all of their former lands, privileges, laws and customs'.
1752: New Serbia is settled on the north-western Zaporozhian lands.

wars.name: Russo-Polish War (1654-1667)
wars.outcome: The Truce of Andrusovo, signed 9 February 1667 (O.S.

wars.name: Battle of Poltava
wars.outcome: The Zaporozhian Host under Kost Hordiienko joined Hetman Ivan Mazepa against Russia; after the Russian victory Peter ordered a retaliatory destruction of the Sich (Chortomlyk), and the Host moved to the Kamianka Sich.

wars.name: Pruth campaign and Treaty of the Pruth
wars.outcome: Treaty signed 23 July 1711 on the river Prut: Azov returned to the Ottoman Empire, Taganrog and several fortresses (Kodak, Novobogoroditskaya, Kamenny Zaton on the Dnieper) to be demolished.

wars.name: Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich
wars.outcome: Russian forces under Peter Tekeli surrounded the Sich on 5 June 1775; the manifesto of 3 August 1775 disbanded the Host and annexed its lands to the Novorossiya Governorate; the Sich was razed and the Cossacks fled to the Danube Delta.

certainty.note: Only a core round the lower Dnieper is drawn; the pages give no boundary, and the Sich page says 'no formal boundaries are stated' for the Free Lands.
The Liberties had no surveyed boundary on the pages opened (only river mouths and the rapids).
